title: The talk's site: the highlights
sub: A debrief of presentation.sgit.ai, for the editor, from the librarian's study
made_from: index/talk-site/ at 2426adc (the librarian's first pass, 30 October 2026, 16:13 to 16:31 UTC): its list of the best things, its verdicts and its screenshots, of the published site at release v0.2.1 (the talk's repository at 424b67a, which is 298be4e plus three commits added after the day).
how: Each highlight: what it is, why it matters to the book, and where it lives. The screenshots are the librarian's, the first screen of each page; the words on why it matters are the designer's reading, for the editor to weigh. The keys and vaults pages are described, not shown. No number appears here that is not on a screenshot.

highlights.title: The home page's three circles
highlights.what: The insider, the infrastructure and the decision as a Venn diagram, with the scenario in the overlap.
highlights.why: The talk's whole argument in one picture: the book's opening could carry it, redrawn in the book's palette.

highlights.title: The talk as web pages, with a player
highlights.what: Every slide a page that animates, a timer, presenter notes behind one key, a slide grid.
highlights.why: The deck is a website anyone can read: the evidence for 'Building the talk', and the reason the book can cite slides by address.

highlights.title: Three known problems. One perfect storm.
highlights.what: The opening slide: the circles drawn one at a time.
highlights.why: The same idea as the home page, in motion: a candidate for the lab's three-frame treatment.

highlights.title: A reasoning engine in a loop, with tools
highlights.what: The definition of an agent as three boxes on a circle, sourced on the slide.
highlights.why: The book's definition of an agent, already drawn and already cited: the simplest figure to carry over.

highlights.title: The dashboard
highlights.what: The team's state read from its own files: a London clock, any hold, what waits on the editor.
highlights.why: It still shows the night's last hold. 'Pause all actions' opens on this panel.

highlights.title: The public vaults page
highlights.what: Each vault's read key as text and as a QR code, under a red box: every file in these vaults is public, forever.
highlights.why: The plainest statement of what 'public' meant on the day; the book discusses it without reprinting a key, so it is not shown here.

highlights.title: The key register
highlights.what: Every member's fingerprint, encryption key and session, with the rule 'the push is the authorisation'.
highlights.why: Identity as a published record: the mechanism behind 'A mandate you can read'. Described, not shown, like the vaults page.

highlights.title: Who builds this site
highlights.what: One card per member: its role, its last wake in one line, its key and how many paths it may write.
highlights.why: The team as a page: 'The hourly machine' in one screen, and a model for this book's own team page.

highlights.title: The explained animations
highlights.what: ruv-sgit's pieces, each with a frame-by-frame explainer and the data it was drawn from; the blast radius shown.
highlights.why: The richest visual material of the day, already explained; the lab's next experiments start here.

highlights.title: Meet the team (M03)
highlights.what: The agents and the editor as an orbit, the prelude to part 1.
highlights.why: The schedule as a picture: a clock face the book's cast already borrows (the conductor's face).

highlights.title: The storyteller's Wardley maps
highlights.what: Pioneers, settlers and town planners, with 'positions, not measurements' on the slide.
highlights.why: RC1 already carries Wardley maps of its own; these are where they came from.

highlights.title: The editor approves each policy, item by item
highlights.what: The review page the editor used for ruv-sgit's policy, as a slide.
highlights.why: 'The editor signs' made visible: the one screen where a person approves what an agent may do.

highlights.title: One action's journey
highlights.what: An agent's request, its policy row, the decision and its receipt, in three acts: allowed, denied, sent to a human.
highlights.why: A control explained as a story with an ending: the model for the lab's 'control, before and after'.

highlights.title: The studio
highlights.what: A brief per part of the argument, several versions side by side, the best promoted into the deck.
highlights.why: How the talk's visuals were chosen, which is how the lab chooses: try several, keep one, record the rest.

highlights.title: The night, and the talk, in pictures
highlights.what: Two long articles: the night hour by hour, and the talk as given (added after the day, a9c0b49).
highlights.why: The day's record already laid out as reading; the book's timeline and chapter 10 can cite them page by page.
